title: 2024 Alaska Air Fuel Douglas C-54 crash
summary: A Douglas C-54D carrying fuel from Fairbanks to Kobuk experienced failure of the left outboard engine shortly after takeoff. When the crew attempted to feather the failed engine's propeller, a maintenance defect in the feathering system allowed pressurized oil to spray onto the hot exhaust, igniting a fire. Fuel that had leaked from a damaged tank behind the engine subsequently exploded, severing aileron controls and forcing an uncontrolled descent into terrain.
probable_cause: Maintenance error in improper installation of the feathering system nut and failure to adequately repair a fuel tank leak, leading to inflight fire and loss of control when the pilot attempted to feather the failed engine. (Preliminary NTSB Form 6120.1)

factors.evidence: A fuel leak had developed in the outboard fuel tank of the left wing near engine one with fuel dripping at between five and ten drops of fuel per minute (p. 2, summary record).

The AN bulkhead fitting had a B-nut installed, but it was not attached to the corresponding oil hose for the feathering system, a critical safety component (p. 1-2, narrative). Engine was a newly rebuilt engine from Anderson Aeromotive with approximately seven hours total time since installation (p. 8).
Engine one lost power shortly after takeoff at approximately 1000 local time (p. 4, form data; p. 1, summary record).

Fire developed in or behind engine #1 shortly after engine failure was indicated; fire appears to have penetrated the #1 rear firewall and reached the #2 (inboard) main wing fuel tank (p. 1, narrative). Bright explosion was captured on video coming from the engine area (p. 1, summary record).
Aircraft entered a sharp left turn and began an uncontrolled descent following the engine fire and fuel tank explosion (p. 1, summary record).
The failing engine separated from the aircraft approximately 100 feet above the ground; fuel tank explosion severed aileron controls (p. 1-2, summary record).

events.text: Aircraft departed from Fairbanks Airport (PAFA) bound for Kobuk at approximately 0955 local time with fuel cargo load of 7,400 gallons 100LL avgas (p. 4, form data).
Smoke observed from engine one which was no longer operating; engine failure indicated on tracking data approximately 8 minutes after takeoff (p. 1, narrative).

White smoke and fire developed behind the engine with bright explosion captured on video; fire originated from pressurized oil from the feathering system nut (improperly installed) spraying onto hot exhaust surfaces (p. 1-2, narrative and summary).
Fire penetrated the #1 rear firewall and reached the #2 (inboard) main wing fuel tank causing that wing tank to explode in flight (p. 1, narrative).
Aircraft entered a sharp left turn following the explosion and began an uncontrolled descent (p. 1, summary record).
The failing engine separated from the aircraft approximately 100 feet above the ground (p. 1, summary record).

Infrasound data recorded the aircraft impacting terrain near Tanana River approximately 8 minutes and 8 seconds after departure with two occupants aboard; aircraft destroyed on impact (p. 1, summary record).

recommendations.text: Safety recommendations to follow after investigation of the #1 engine and wing area.
